costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM654 engine typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this updated engine is the condition of the 48V mild-hybrid starter-generator (ISG), the AdBlue dosing module, and the EGR cooler. failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM654.930/940 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System Faults
items.whatHappens: The AdBlue dosing module, heater, or NOx sensors can fail, leading to warning lights, restricted performance (limp mode), and eventually a no-start condition if the tank is depleted and the system is locked out by the ECU.
items.repairVsReplace: Often resolved by replacing the dosing module or NOx sensor, which is a standard repair. If the tank heater or pump has failed, a full tank assembly replacement may be required.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The internal matrix of the EGR cooler can crack, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases or enter the intake manifold. This leads to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock if severe.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard repair. If caught early, it prevents catastrophic internal engine damage.

items.title: Mild-Hybrid (ISG) Integration Issues
items.whatHappens: The Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) is a complex 48V component. While generally reliable, software glitches or electrical faults can cause start-stop malfunctions, reduced EQ Boost assistance, or warning lights.
items.repairVsReplace: Most ISG issues are resolved via software updates or replacing the 48V auxiliary battery. Full ISG replacement is rare but costly if the unit itself fails.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM654.930/940 is considered highly robust, building on the already solid OM651 and early OM654 foundation. Units maintained with strict AdBlue top-ups and regular oil changes routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM654.930/940
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM654.930 and .940 are the updated, mild-hybrid variants of the OM654 family. They are sometimes confused with the earlier non-hybrid OM654.920/921 or the older OM651.911/912. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM654.930/940 features a 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), distinct wiring looms, and specific ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with an earlier OM654 or OM651 without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM654.930/940 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM654.930/940 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof that the AdBlue system, EGR cooler, and 48V ISG are in good working order. Given the complexity of modern hybrid emissions systems, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM654 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by verifying the AdBlue dosing module, replacing the EGR cooler, and refreshing all critical seals, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM654 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage W213 E-Class or X254 GLC hosts where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM654 engine is installed by specialists familiar with modern Mercedes CDI and mild-hybrid systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM654.930/940 is typically found in modern W206, W213, and X254 vehicles valued between £15,000 and £45,000, a full replacement is highly financially viable and comfortably within the host vehicle's value . Replacement cost rarely exceeds the scrap threshold for these modern chassis, making a reconditioned unit a highly sensible investment.
